stemMd: The student wants to emphasise the size of the difference between the two groups of marshes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Tidal marshes store carbon in waterlogged soil, where decay proceeds slowly.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Marshes restored more than 30 years earlier stored 4.6 kilograms of carbon per square metre, nearly four times the 1.2 kilograms stored by marshes restored fewer than 10 years earlier.

options.label: C
options.textMd: In 2023, ecologist Hana Vrbova surveyed 32 restored tidal marshes along a single coastline.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Vrbova concluded that carbon storage in a restored tidal marsh builds up slowly over the course of decades.

explanationMd:
A rhetorical-synthesis item is scored against the stated goal, not against general quality. The goal here is to emphasise *the size of a difference*, so the winning sentence must put both figures side by side and make the gap visible.

Choice B does all of that: it gives 4.6 kg/m² and 1.2 kg/m², and it quantifies the relationship. Check the multiplier: $4.6 \div 1.2 \approx 3.83$, so "nearly four times" is accurate and does not overstate the notes.

To check any synthesis answer, underline the goal's key words — here "the size of the difference" — and confirm the sentence contains both sides of the comparison. Only B does.

distractorRationale.a: Accurate, but it gives background on how marshes store carbon and mentions neither group of marshes. A sentence with no comparison in it cannot emphasise the size of a difference.
distractorRationale.c: Accurate, but it emphasises the scope of the survey — the year and the 32 sites. Study size is a different rhetorical goal from the magnitude of the result.
distractorRationale.d: This states the conclusion drawn from the difference rather than the difference itself. "Slowly over decades" describes the pattern qualitatively and includes neither of the two storage figures.

accessibilityText: Using the five student notes about carbon in restored tidal marshes, choose the sentence that best emphasises the size of the difference between marshes restored recently and marshes restored long ago.

provenance.notes: Original item built on the original notes stimulus.

review.author: digital-sat-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Only (b) gives both group values and quantifies the gap: 4.6 against 1.2 kg per square metre, or 4.6/1.2, about 3.8, which is 'nearly four times'. (a) is general background. (c) describes the survey. (d) states the conclusion without showing how large the difference is.
